DEFINITION

SINGLE POLE DOUBLE THROW SWITCH (SPDT) - A single pole switch is one that opens or closes one circuit or current path. A double throw switch is one that the arm or activator can connect to two different stationary contacts.
The relay contacts are called normally open (NO) and normally closed (NC). This refers to their state when the relay is de-energized.
A Control Relay is a magnetically operated switch that directs signals. Each set of contacts is similar to a single pole double throw switch (SPDT)..

When a voltage is applied to the coil a magnetic field is produced and the relay is closed, operating like a closed switch. The relay is referred to as energized.
When there is no voltage applied to the coil no magnetic field is produced and the relay is open, operating like an open switch. The relay is referred to as de-energized.
DEFINITION

SINGLE POLE SINGLE THROW (SPST) SWITCH - A single pole switch is one that opens or closes one circuit or current path. A single throw switch is a switch with only one moving arm and one stationary contact.
The magnetic coil opens and closes the contacts when voltage is applied to it or removed from it.
